title: Coordinate hyperplane as projective space
statement: For the coordinate data [def-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-data], over any field K and n ≥ 1, the zero subscheme of T_0 in projective n-space is relative projective (n-1)-space over K. The chosen isomorphism commutes with the structural morphisms to Spec K. When n=0 no hyperplane assertion is required.

proof.text: Define the graded coordinate-deletion map by T_i ↦ 0 and T_j ↦ T_j for j ≠ i. Renaming the remaining variables splits it, so it is surjective. Its kernel is the principal ideal (T_i): after quotienting by T_i, the rename followed by deletion is the identity. Proj therefore gives a closed immersion from the integral projective space on the remaining coordinates; pull it back to Spec K. The image consists precisely of homogeneous primes containing T_i, by the prime ideal correspondence for a surjective ring map. The nonvanishing-locus equation for the coordinate section identifies this image with the support of its zero scheme.

On the jth standard affine chart the zero-locus ideal is generated by the ratio T_i/T_j, using the free twist generator and the section equation. If i=j this is the unit ideal. Otherwise the polynomial chart-ring equivalence identifies it with a variable ideal, whose quotient is a polynomial ring over K and whose primality follows also from the kernel of coordinate deletion. Each local ideal is radical; affine-cover extensionality proves the global ideal is radical. Projective space on the remaining coordinates is reduced, since its standard affine charts are polynomial rings over K. The kernel of its closed embedding is therefore the vanishing ideal of its image. It equals the radical zero-locus ideal, hence the zero-locus ideal itself. The closed-immersion lifting API now supplies an isomorphism from the zero subscheme to projective space on the remaining coordinates, with its factorization equation.

Reindex the n remaining coordinates by ULift (Fin n), using the graded polynomial rename maps in both directions. Their composites are identities, hence the induced Proj and base-changed scheme maps are inverse. Apply the free-module comparison of lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry to identify the stipulated relative projective (n-1)-space with the same polynomial projective space. Compose these isomorphisms and their over-base equations. The arithmetic n-1+1=n follows from n≥1. When n=0 the hyperplane field is indexed by an impossible inequality and requires no witness. Choice of these isomorphisms occurs inside the proof of Nonempty, never inside a definition.
